{{short description|German mathematician and Jesuit}}
[[File:Lantz_-_Institutionum_arithmeticarum_libri_quatuor,_1619_-_193839.jpg|thumb|''Institutionum arithmeticarum libri quatuor'', 1619]]
'''Johann Lantz''' or '''Lanz''' (1564 – 20 September 1638) was a German [[mathematician]] and [[Jesuit]].<ref name="Ingaliso2005" /><ref name="Feingold2003" />

== Biography ==
Born in [[Tettnang]] on [[Lake Constance]] in 1564, he was admitted as [[novice]] in [[Landsberg am Lech|Landsberg]] in 1589.<ref name="Ingaliso2005">{{cite book|author=Luigi Ingaliso|title=Filosofia e cosmologia in Christoph Scheiner|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AAZ-EY1XQTYC&pg=PA63|year=2005|publisher=Rubbettino Editore|language=it|isbn=978-88-498-1258-9|page=63}}</ref>
He became a professor of [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] at the [[University of Ingolstadt]]. After 1609-1610 he left his place to his pupil [[Christoph Scheiner]]<ref name="Feingold2003">{{cite book|author=Mordechai Feingold|title=Jesuit Science and the Republic of Letters|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oSSEpTB15VEC&pg=PA33|year=2003|publisher=MIT Press|language=en|isbn=978-0-262-06234-3|page=33}}</ref> and moved to [[Munich]], where he died in 1638.<ref name="Ingaliso2005" />

He wrote several works on mathematics. He analyzed the four genres of numbers, then the astronomic fractions.<ref name="Ingaliso2005" /> He is remembered also by [[Mario Bettini]] in his ''Aerarium philosophiae mathematicae'' (1648).<ref name="Ingaliso2005" /><ref>{{cite book|publisher=typis Io.
